research_caveat: TWO MAJOR CAVEATS. (1) NETWORK: the sandbox gateway (agent proxy) returned 403 CONNECT denials for Meta-owned domains (llama.developer.meta.com; curl and WebFetch both blocked) in this session, so no page could be fetched directly. Every value below is sourced from Meta's own pages as returned verbatim in domain-restricted web-search snippets (allowed_domains limited to llama.developer.meta.com / ai.meta.com / llama.com / developer.meta.com / facebook.com / meta.com / about.fb.com). Per researcher hard rules, confidence is capped at 'low' even where the underlying Meta documentation is unambiguous; the verifier should re-fetch each source_url from an unrestricted network. (2) SERVICE SHUT DOWN: Meta's own deprecation notice (https://llama.developer.meta.com/docs/llama-api-deprecation/, 'Upcoming changes to Llama API') states the Llama API public preview WOUND DOWN ON JULY 6, 2026 — i.e. BEFORE today (2026-07-31); on that date the service shuts down and API requests return a sunset response. If Tavus's use of Meta was via the Llama API, Meta may no longer be an active sub-processor at all, and this column may belong OFF the form (or annotated as terminated) rather than filled in. A human must confirm whether Tavus still sends any data to Meta before this vendor is written into the workbook.

3.1.1.locator: Llama API Terms of Service / Llama API product page (developer.meta.com/ai/products/llama-api/): 'your data is encrypted in transit and at rest using industry-standard security'
3.1.1.notes: Real standard for 'indicate below': Meta documents only that Llama API data is 'encrypted in transit ... using industry-standard security' — no TLS version is published for the Llama API service, and the dropdown has no 'Not known' option for this row, so 'Others' with this note is the honest choice. Do NOT use: (a) the TLS 1.3/mTLS material at llama.com/docs/deployment/security-in-production/ — that is a deployment guide for customer SELF-HOSTED/private-cloud Llama, not the Meta-operated API; (b) the 'TLS 1.2 or equivalent' language in Meta's developer Data Security Requirements (developers.facebook.com) — those are requirements Meta imposes on THIRD-PARTY app developers, not statements about Meta's own service. Meta's own Data Security Terms (facebook.com/legal/terms/data_security_terms) say Meta enforces 'appropriate protocols designed to protect the confidentiality of data in transit over public networks' — again no version. Snippet-sourced; direct fetches blocked.

3.1.2.locator: Llama API Terms of Service / Llama API product page: 'your data is encrypted in transit and at rest using industry-standard security'; ToS Data Security statements: 'Data processed by the Llama API is stored separately from other Meta product data'
3.1.2.notes: Encryption at rest IS affirmed by Meta for the Llama API, but the algorithm/standard (AES-128/192/256 etc.) is not published anywhere retrieved this session, so the standard itself is 'Not known'. Do not upgrade to AES-256 from industry norms. The CMK/envelope-encryption content on llama.com/docs/deployment/ pages describes customer self-hosted deployments, not the Meta-operated API. Ask vendor for the algorithm.

3.1.3.notes: Backup encryption is not documented separately for the Llama API on any Meta primary source found this session. Searched: llama.developer.meta.com terms-of-service, developer.meta.com/ai/products/llama-api/, facebook.com/legal/terms/data_security_terms, facebook.com/legal/terms/Privacy/TOMs (all via domain-restricted search snippets; direct fetches blocked by gateway 403). Per the field playbook, 'Not known' is common and correct here.

3.1.4.notes: No Meta primary source retrieved this session states who generates/holds the encryption keys for Llama API data at rest, and no CMEK/BYOK offering is documented for the Llama API. The playbook's default for managed cloud ('Key generated by Subprocessor (not customer-specific)') is an inference from industry norms, which the hard rules forbid — leaving 'Not known' and asking the vendor. Searched the same Llama API ToS / product / Data Security Terms pages as 3.1.1-3.1.3.

3.1.6.locator: Meta Global Processor Terms (MGPT), General Terms: 'Meta may de-identify and anonymize Applicable Personal Data received from Company under the Applicable Terms and Process such data as permitted by Applicable Law'. The Llama API ToS separately states Meta 'may aggregate and anonymize data relating to how developers interact with the Services' and use it for business purposes
3.1.6.notes: The MGPT is incorporated by reference into the Llama API Terms of Service, so this is the applicable processor contract. It documents an anonymization capability/right on Applicable Personal Data. Note the nuance: this is Meta's right to anonymize for its own permitted purposes, not necessarily an on-request anonymization service for the customer — flagged in open questions. Snippet-sourced; direct fetch blocked (gateway 403).

3.1.7.notes: No Meta primary source retrieved this session states a pseudonymization capability for Llama API / processor data. The MGPT language found says 'de-identify and anonymize' — de-identification is not the same as GDPR pseudonymization and equating them would be inference. Meta's TOMs page (facebook.com/legal/terms/Privacy/TOMs) surfaced access-control, physical-security and transit-encryption measures in snippets but no pseudonymization statement. Searched: facebook.com/legal/terms/Meta-Global-Processor-Terms/, facebook.com/legal/terms/Privacy/TOMs, facebook.com/legal/terms/data_security_terms, llama.developer.meta.com/legal/terms-of-service.
